The present petition has been instituted under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973, read with Article 227 of the Constitution of India, seeking the following reliefs "A.

That the Hon'ble Court be pleased to call for record and proceedings of Criminal Case No.536 of 2010 from the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate First Class, Himmatnagar and be pleased to quash and set aside the complaint and all orders passed against the applicants therein including the order dated 23.2.2010 issuing the summoning to the applicant.

entities.text: Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate First Class, Himmatnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: B. That Pending the hearing and final disposal of this application, the Hon'ble Court be pleased to stay further proceedings of Criminal Case of 536 of 2010 pending in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate First Class, Himmatnagar."

BRIEF FACTS OF THE CASE:-
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15035/2013 ORDER DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined 2.

The applicants have preferred the present petition seeking quashment of Criminal Case No. 536 of 2010 pending before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Himmatnagar, arising out of a complaint filed by respondent No.2.

entities.text: Chief Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Himmatnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The gravamen of the complaint pertains to the collection of a drug, namely Pimpless Cream, from Shah Jivraj Gulabchand & Company, Himmatnagar on 02.08.2006, which upon analysis by the Government Analyst was reported, vide report dated 22.05.2007, to be not of standard quality.

It is alleged therein that the said drug was manufactured by M/s. Preet Remedies Pvt. Ltd., Baddi (Himachal Pradesh), and that applicant No.1 - Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd. had purchased the said drug under invoice dated 20.06.2006, and thereafter sold it to Noble Remedies, who in turn sold it to Rajendra Drug House, Ahmedabad, from whom Shah Jivraj Gulabchand & Company purchased the same under invoice dated 12.07.2006.

It is also on record that the Health and Family Welfare Department, Himachal Pradesh, by order dated 26.02.2009, suspended the licence of the manufacturer - M/s. Preet Remedies Pvt. Ltd. - for a period of ninety days with effect from 01.03.2009.
2.1.

entities.text: Health and Family Welfare Department, Himachal Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Significantly, the complaint contains no specific allegations against applicant Nos. 2 to 9, who are merely joined as Directors of applicant No.1, without any averment that they were in charge of,
or responsible for, the conduct of business of the company at the relevant time.
It is further an admitted position that the drug in question was not manufactured by applicant No.1.
The complainant, moreover, failed to issue any statutory intimation to the applicants as contemplated under Section 25(3) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.

Notwithstanding the absence of such foundational averments, the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate issued process on 23.02.2010,
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15035/2013 ORDER DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined and upon service of summons dated 04.01.2013, the present petitioners entered appearance before the Trial Court and, after collecting the requisite papers, have invoked the inherent jurisdiction of this Court for quashing of the impugned proceedings.
SUBMISSION OF THE PETITIONER:-
3. Learned Senior Advocate, Mr. Mihir Joshi, assisted by learned Advocate, Ms. Krisha Bhimani,
appearing for the petitioners, has submitted, in the first instance, that a plain reading of the private complaint would reveal that no specific allegations have been levelled against Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd. or any of its directors. Drawing the Court's attention to the complaint, Mr. Joshi,
learned Senior Advocate submitted that the solitary averment therein is that Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd. had obtained sub-standard drugs under Invoice No. 908 dated 20.06.2006, and apart from the said assertion, there are no other allegations implicating the petitioners.

In support of this proposition, reliance has been placed upon the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of Haryana v. Brij Lal Mittal & Ors., (1998) 5 SCC 343.
Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd vs State Of Gujarat on 20 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148104524/
2 3.1.

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Brij Lal Mittal & Ors., (1998) 5 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd vs State Of Gujarat on 20 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Secondly, it has been contended that the petitioners-accused are residing beyond the territorial jurisdiction of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Himatnagar.

In such circumstances, it is urged that, in view of the mandate of Section 202 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the learned Magistrate was bound to conduct an inquiry, postponing the issuance of process, before summoning the accused.
Failure to do so amounts to a manifest non-compliance of Section 202 Cr.P.C.
It is submitted that learned Chief Judicial Magistrate has issued process without conducting inquiry under Section 202.
Thus, issuance of process is legally unjustifiable.

In fortification of this NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15035/2013 ORDER DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined submission,
learned Senior Advocate has placed reliance on the recent pronouncement of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in JM Laboratories & Ors. v. State of Andhra Pradesh & Anr., 2025 SCC OnLine SC 208.
3.2.

entities.text: JM Laboratories & Ors. v. State of Andhra Pradesh & Anr., 2025 SCC OnLine SC 208
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the strength of the above submissions, learned Senior Advocate Mr. Joshi has earnestly prayed that the impugned order of issuance of process against the petitioners deserves to be set aside.

SUBMISSION OF THE RESPONDENT:-
4. Learned APP, on the other hand, having adverted to the complaint, submitted that M/s. Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd. had procured sub-standard drugs from Preet Remedies Pvt. Ltd., with full knowledge that the drugs so purchased were indeed sub- standard.

It was thus urged that the factual allegations, as they stand, prima facie attract the offences punishable under Sections 18(a)(i),
18(a)(vi) and 27 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.

4.1. It was further contended by the learned APP that the defences sought to be canvassed by the petitioners are matters touching disputed questions of fact, which can only be adjudicated upon evidence during the course of trial.
At this incipient stage, such contentions cannot be permitted to thwart the criminal process or to scuttle the complaint at its very threshold.
4.2. In view of the aforesaid submissions, learned APP has prayed for dismissal of the present petition.

FINDINGS, ANALYSIS AND CONCLUSION OF  COURT:-

sentences.text: I have heard learned advocates appearing for both sides and have carefully perused the complaint as well as the material placed on record.

The complaint filed by the Drug Inspector, which is placed at page 14 of the paper-book, came to be instituted before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Himatnagar, and has been registered as Criminal Case No. 536 of 2010.
5.2. Upon issuance of process, it transpires from the complaint that the firm, Preet Remedies, is alleged to have manufactured sub- standard drugs.
In paragraph 8 of the complaint, it is specifically alleged that M/s. Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd. procured such sub-standard drugs under Invoice No. 908 dated 20.06.2006.

The complaint has been instituted invoking Sections 18(a)(i)
and 18(a)
(vi) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, alleging breach thereof, which is punishable under Section 27 of the said Act.

5.3. A plain reading of the complaint, in its entirety, and on face indicates that the only allegation levelled against M/s. Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd. is that it had purchased sub-standard drugs from Preet Remedies, with full knowledge of the fact that the drugs so purchased were sub-standard in nature.

Indeed, the entire basis for arraigning M/s. Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd. as an accused rests on the following three lines contained in the complaint, translated from the vernacular, which read thus:
"M/s. Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd., Vadodara, has procured the said medicine from M/s. Preet Remedies Pvt. Ltd., HPSIDC Industrial Area, Baddi (Himachal Pradesh), under Invoice No. 908 dated 20.06.2006."

6. In the aforesaid backdrop, the provisions of Sections 18(a)(i) NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15035/2013 ORDER DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined and 18(a)(vi) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, which are germane to the controversy, are reproduced hereinbelow:-
Section 18(a)(i) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940:-
"(a)manufacture for sale or for distribution, or sell, or stock or exhibit or offer for sale, or distribute-- (i)any drug which is not of a standard quality, or is misbranded, adulterated or spurious;"
Section 18(a)(vi) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940:-

"(a)manufacture for sale or for distribution, or sell, or stock or exhibit or offer for sale, or distribute-- Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd vs State Of Gujarat on 20 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148104524/
4 (vi) any drug or cosmetic in contravention of any of the provisions of this Chapter or any rule made thereunder;"
6.1.

entities.text:
Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd vs State Of Gujarat on 20 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148104524/
4 (vi)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There exists, under the scheme of the Act, a clear prohibition on the manufacture and sale of drugs and cosmetics which are not of standard quality or which fall within the mischief of being sub- standard.
Any contravention thereof would inevitably invite the penal consequences contemplated under Section 27(d) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.

6.2. However, the moot question that arises is whether M/s. Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd. had,
with conscious knowledge, either purchased or sold any sub-standard drug.
The complaint, as it stands, does not provide a categorical answer to this crucial aspect.

6.3. The only indication emerging from the record is that M/s.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15035/2013 ORDER DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd. had procured the drug from Preet Remedies Pvt. Ltd. under Invoice No.
908 dated 20.06.2006.
Beyond this recital, there is no material to demonstrate that M/s. Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd. had any intent to purchase or to trade in sub-standard drugs.
If indeed such an intention were attributable, the complaint ought to have contained clear and specific averments to that effect, which are conspicuously absent.

7. In view of the foregoing discussion, compelling M/s. Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd. to stand trial in the absence of requisite material would amount to nothing short of an abuse of the process of law.

8. At this stage, it would be apposite to advert to Section 34 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940,
which delineates the liability of companies in respect of offences, and the said provision reads as under:-
"34. Offences by companies.--
( 1)Where
an offence under this Act has been committed by a company

, every person who at the time the offence was committed, was in charge of, and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly:Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall render any such person liable to any punishment provided in this Act if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge or that he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence.

(2)Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company and it is proved that the offence has been committed with the consent or connivance of, or is attributable to any neglect on the part of, any director, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15035/2013 ORDER DATED:
Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd vs State Of Gujarat on 20 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148104524/
5 20/08/2025 undefined manager, secretary or other officer of the company, such director, manager, secretary or other officer shall also be deemed to be guilty of that offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly."
8.1.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In order to arraign a Director of the company as an accused, it is incumbent, at least prima facie,
to establish that such Director was in charge of and responsible for the conduct of the business of the company at the relevant time.
Alternatively, it must be demonstrated that the alleged offence was committed with the consent, connivance, or attributable negligence on the part of the said Director.

9. In the case of State of Haryana v. Brij Lal Mittal (supra), the Apex Court addressed the issue,
relevant paras are as under:-
8.

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Brij Lal Mittal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Nonetheless, we find that the impugned judgment of the High Court has got to be upheld for an altogether different reason.

Admittedly, the three respondents were being prosecuted as rectors of the manufacturers with the aid of Section 34(1) of the act which reads as under:-
"34. Offences by companies: - (1) Where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company/every person who at the time the offence was committed,
was in charge of, and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company shall be deemed to be quality, of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.

Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall render any such person liable to any punishment NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15035/2013 ORDER DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined provided in this Act if he proves that the offence was committed without its knowledge or that he exercised at due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence."

It is thus seen that the vicarious liability of a person for being prosecuted for an offence committed under the Act by a company arises if at the material time he was in-charge of and was also responsible to the company for the conduct of its business.
Simply because a person is a director of the company it does not necessarily mean that he fulfills both the above requirements so as to make him liable.
Conversely, without being a director a person can be in- charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of its business.

From the complaint in question we, however, find that except a baid statement that the respondents were directors of the manufacturers, there is no other allegation to indicate, even prima facie, that they were in-charge of the company and also responsible to the company for the conduct of its business.

9. In Delhi Municipality vs. Ram Kishan [(1983) 1 S.C.C.1] while dealing with the applicability of Section 17(1) of the Prevention of the Food Adulteration Act, 1954, which is in pari materia with Section 34(1) of the Act, on similar facts, this Court observed as under:

6

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: STATUTE

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "So far as the Manager is concerned, we are satisfied that from the very nature of his duties it can be safely inferred that he would undoubtedly be vicariously liable for the offence, Various liability being and incident of an offence under the Act.

So far as the Directors are concerned, there is not even a whisper not a shred of evidence nor anything to show, apart from the presumption drawn by the complainant, that there is any act committed by the Directors from which a reasonable inference can be drawn that they could also be vicariously liable.

In these circumstances, therefore, we find ourselves in complete agreement with the argument of the High Court that no case against the Directors (accused Nos. 4 to 7) has been made out ex facie on the allegations made in the complaint and the proceedings against them were rightly quashed."

NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15035/2013 ORDER DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined (emphasis supplied)
10.

Since we are in respectful agreement with the view si expressed we dismiss this appeal and uphold the order of the High Court quashing the prosecution against the three respondents on a different ground."
10. Applying the aforesaid ratio to the facts of the present case, this Court is of the considered view that the prosecution of the Director of M/s. Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd., in the absence of any specific allegation or prima facie material demonstrating that he was in charge of and responsible for the day-to-day affairs of the company, cannot be sustained for the alleged contravention of Sections 18(a)(i) and 18(a)(vi) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.
11.

Non compliance of the Section 202 of the Cr.PC is also argued, which is as under:-
Any Magistrate, on receipt of a complaint of an offence of which he is authorised to take cognizance or which has been made over to him under section 192 may, if he thinks fit, [and shall, in a case where the accused is residing at a place beyond the area in which he exercises his jurisdiction] [Inserted by Act 25 of 2005, Section 19 (w.e.f. 23-6-2006).] postpone the issue of process against the accused, and either inquire into the case himself or direct an investigation to be made by a police officer or by such other person as he thinks fit, for the purpose of deciding whether or not there is sufficient ground for proceeding :
Provided that no such direction for investigation shall be made, -
(a)where it appears to the Magistrate that the offence NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15035/2013 ORDER DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined complained of is triable exclusively by the Court of Session;
or Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd vs State Of Gujarat on 20 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148104524/
7 (b)where the complaint has not been made by a Court, unless the complainant and the witnesses present (if any) have been examined on oath under section 200.

entities.text: or Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(2)In an inquiry under sub-section (1), the Magistrate may, if he thinks fit, take evidence of witnesses on oath :
Provided that if it appears to the Magistrate that the offence complained of is triable exclusively by the Court of Session, he shall call upon the complainant to produce all his witnesses and examine them on oath.

(3)If an investigation under sub-section (1) is made by a person not being a police officer, he shall have for that investigation all the powers conferred by this Court on an officer-in-charge of a police station except the power to arrest without warrant."
12.
It is manifest from the record that the accused are residing beyond the territorial jurisdiction of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Himatnagar.

In such circumstances, it was incumbent upon the learned Trial Court, in faithful compliance with the mandate of Section 202 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, to postpone the issuance of process and to conduct the requisite inquiry before summoning the accused.

The failure to do so amounts to a serious jurisdictional infirmity, as has been unequivocally enunciated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in JM Laboratories (supra).
CONCLUSION:-
13.
By order dated 16.08.2025, this Court has already abated the petition qua petitioner Nos. 3, 5, 6 and 9.

Accordingly, in the final NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15035/2013 ORDER DATED:
20/08/2025 undefined reckoning, the petition qua petitioner Nos. 3, 5, 6 and 9 stands abated.
Insofar as the remaining petitioners are concerned, the petition is ALLOWED.

The order of issuance of process against the said petitioners in Criminal Case No.536 of 2010 pending before Chief Judicial Magistrate, Himmatnagar as well as all consequential proceedings arising therefrom, is hereby quashed and set aside.
14.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.
